summary: The agency acknowledged both issues raised by manufacturers — the appropriate standard level and the possible separate classification of four-wheel-drive general utility vehicles — and stated it had not yet reached a final decision, choosing instead to analyze a range of fuel economy levels and two NPA classes in the final EIS.
text:
Comments to the proposed fuel economy have been received and are being analyzed. The comments received have raised

two basic issues: the appropriate level for the MY 1979 standard, and whether to create a separate classification of nonpassenger automobiles which are four wheel drive, general utility vehicles. Virtually all manufacturers of nonpassenger automobiles who submitted comments indicated their belief that the level of the standard was too high, in light of the effects of emissions and other factors. Also, several commenters indicated that four wheel drive, general utility vehicles had special fuel economy characteristics which entitle them to separate treatment from other nonpassenger automobiles. Obviously, the agency has not had time to reach a final decision on either of these issues. Therefore, the final environmental impact statement will consider the environmental and resource impacts that will result from a range of levels of fuel economy standards, and from alternative decisions on the classification issue. This approach will enable both the Administrator and the public to see the relative environmental impacts resulting from the choice of one course of action over alternative choices.
